title: IDTM Maintenance Instructions
overview: Complete guide for preventive and corrective maintenance of the IDTM (Infectious Disease Treatment Module) based on the AZF4-27 Inflatable Tent system. This guide covers maintenance during operations, before storage, during storage, and repair procedures.

sections.title: Preventive Maintenance Instructions (PMIs)
sections.description: Scheduled maintenance tasks to prevent issues and extend tent lifespan

steps.title: PMI 1: Set-up of the Tent
steps.purpose: Ensure proper setup to prevent damage during installation
content: Follow the set-up instructions in the manual
Protect the tent skin from sharp objects in the set-up area
Avoid dragging the tent skin over the ground
Make sure internal objects like furniture do not have pointy or sharp-edged stands
Internal furnishings should not touch the walls and roof of the tent, especially during high winds
Do not leave the tent unattended for long periods of time, as high winds may occur
actions: Inspect set-up area for sharp objects
Position furniture away from tent walls
Assign personnel to monitor tent during setup
warnings: Never drag tent components over the ground
Avoid leaving tent unattended in variable weather

steps.title: PMI 2: Daily Inspection
steps.purpose: Maintain tent condition through regular inspection
content: Protect the tent skin from sharp objects inside
Sweep and/or vacuum-clean the groundsheet
Check whether the zippers are smooth running
Clean zippers from sand and apply dry soap or Teflon-based spray if needed
Check all pegs are solidly anchored and replace them if needed
Arrange for good ventilation to avoid mildew
actions: Sweep or vacuum the groundsheet daily
Test all zippers for smooth operation
warnings: Mildew can develop in poorly ventilated tents
Damaged pegs must be replaced immediately

steps.title: PMI 3: Outstanding Weather Conditions
steps.purpose: Protect tent during adverse weather conditions
steps.pdfStepReference: Windy days, rain, snow, temperature changes | Repair Level 1
content: Wind: Close all openings when wind speed is above 40 km/h
During high winds, regularly check pegs are firmly anchored and guy ropes suitably tensioned
Outside the tent, store away all items that might fly around and damage the tent
Rain: Prevent water from running under tent by digging a small drainage trench
Fasten door threshold in upward position to prevent water from coming inside
Regularly check for water ponding and push away accumulations from inside at an early stage
Snow: Check regularly for snow and ice, remove immediately
Temperature changes: Check pressure of tent frame and reinflate if needed
Check for condensation inside tent and arrange for good ventilation or ACU
Check for ice assemblies on tent and remove immediately
actions: Close all openings above 40 km/h wind
Check peg anchoring during high winds
warnings: Never install tent in winds above 40 km/h
Ice and snow accumulation can damage structure
Water ponding can cause structural issues

steps.title: PMI 4: Dismantling
steps.purpose: Properly dismantle tent to prevent damage
content: Follow the dismantling instructions in the manual
Remove all objects and dirt from inside and outside the tent to avoid damage
Do not drag tent covers over the ground - this may damage the tent skin
The roof covers are easy to fold - if you notice any resistance, stop folding and check for blockages
Avoid packing the tent when wet, humid and/or dirty
If packing wet tent, unpack, clean and dry within 72 hours to avoid mildew
Collect, clean and pack all items, run inventory before loading onto truck
Dismantling is strongly discouraged in case of strong winds or heavy rains
actions: Remove all objects from inside tent
warnings: Never drag tent covers over ground
Wet tents must be dried within 72 hours
Do not dismantle during strong winds or heavy rain

steps.title: PMI 5: Maintenance of Textile Parts
content: Clean all textile parts according to the cleaning instructions (PMI 6)
Clean any special stains from grass, oil, ballpoint pens, etc.
Visually inspect all textile parts for cuts, holes, abrasions, tears, open seams or welded joints
Check whether the fabric needs any repair work
Check for sharp objects inside the tent and remove them
Check all moving parts like zippers by opening and closing them
Pay attention to broken or corroded parts
Check the bags visually for any damage
All parts should be dry before packing
Repack all clean, repaired and complete units on the correct pallets
actions: Test all zippers and moving parts
warnings: Never store wet or damp textiles
Damaged parts must be repaired before storage

steps.title: PMI 6: Cleaning
steps.purpose: Proper cleaning procedures for tent components
content: Use a soft brush (nylon) or sponge
Wash using a water-based detergent solution
For slight dirt: 5% concentration at 20°C
For medium dirt: 10% concentration at 20°C
For stubborn dirt: 10% concentration at 50°C
Rinse with clean water
Difficult deposits may include mineral origin (fats, tars, scale), plant origin (leaves, pollens, resins), or animal origin (bird droppings, crushed insects)
These deposits may require special techniques - contact Lanco for advice before attempting
actions: Use soft nylon brush or sponge
Apply correct concentration based on dirt level
warnings: Do not use harsh chemicals without consulting Lanco
Improper cleaning may damage tent cover

steps.title: PMI 7: Storage Process
steps.purpose: Proper storage procedures to maintain equipment condition
content: All items should always be stored in adequate packaging, away from water and vermin
All items should be cleaned and fully dried before being stored
Check for packing labels and replace missing labels if needed
Make sure packaging units haven't been damaged during transport and/or stacking
The most sensitive items should always be packed on top (e.g., lights)
Make sure no item can fall down during transport or storage condition
actions: Ensure all items are clean and dry
Stack with sensitive items on top
warnings: Never store wet or dirty items
Protect from water and vermin

steps.title: PMI 8: Storage Conditions
content: Ideally storage temperature should be between 18 and 21°C
Air humidity should be between 60% and 65%
The storage area should have good air circulation
No vermin should come into the storage area
warnings: Extreme temperatures can damage materials
High humidity promotes mold and mildew growth

sections.title: Corrective Maintenance Instructions (CMIs)
sections.description: Repair procedures for damages and equipment issues

steps.title: CMI 1: Minor Textile Repairs
steps.purpose: Repair damages smaller than 15cm that do not affect load-bearing parts
steps.pdfStepReference: In case of damage | Minor damages < 15cm
content: Minor damages are damages smaller than 15 cm that do not affect load-bearing parts of the tent skin like attachment points of belts or ropes
Sweep away any dirt/humidity with MEK (methyl ethyl ketone) solvent or methylated spirit
Cut out a patch that overlaps the crack/hole by 3 cm on all sides
Round the corners of the patch
Lay the patch on top of the hole and mark the surrounding
Roughen the area where the patch will be applied using sand paper
Roughen the side of the patch where glue will be applied
Do not touch the clean area with your hands to avoid putting grease on it
Apply glue equally on both areas (patch and damaged area)
Follow the glue's instructions
Wait for the flash-off time
Accurately place the patch on the prepared tent fabric
Press on as hard as you can using a roll, scraper, etc.
Take special care of the rims of the patch
The quality of the gluing only depends on pressure at the beginning
actions: Clean damaged area with MEK or methylated spirit
Cut patch 3cm larger than damage on all sides
Apply glue to both surfaces evenly
Apply firm pressure especially at edges
warnings: MEK and methylated spirits are highly flammable - keep away from naked flames
Do not touch cleaned surfaces with bare hands
Quality depends on initial pressure application

steps.title: CMI 2: Major Textile Repairs
steps.purpose: Handle damages larger than 15cm or affecting load-bearing parts
steps.pdfStepReference: In case of damage | Major damages > 15cm
content: Major damages are damages bigger than 15 cm and/or that affect the load-bearing parts of the tent skin like attachment points of belts, ropes or kedders
Depending on the nature and severity of the damage, additional tools like a sewing machine, hot-air blower or rivet gun etc. might be necessary
Identify the materials needed for repair, contact Lanco for provision of spare parts and repair materials
Close holes and fissures with a repair patch according to CMI 1
If the damage is too important to repair yourself, send the damaged part to Lanco for repair
actions: Contact Lanco for spare parts if needed
Apply patch repair for holes/fissures (per CMI 1)
Send to factory for extensive damage
warnings: Both methylated spirits and MEK are highly flammable - keep away from naked flames
Observe all applicable safety rules when applying glue
Environmental conditions for glue repairs: Temperature > 5°C, Relative humidity < 60%
Major structural repairs should be performed by Lanco

steps.title: CMI 3: Replacement of Frame Parts
content: Locate the source of the leak
In case of a small leak, please refer to CMI 1 for patch repair
In case of extensive damage, order a replacement part arch or beam
Remove the damaged beam from the tent cover, using the wing bolts
Install the new beam, using the wing bolts
actions: Order replacement parts for extensive damage
Remove damaged beam using wing bolts
Install new beam with wing bolts
warnings: Ensure proper fit of replacement parts
Test for leaks after installation

steps.title: CMI 4: Replacement of Missing Parts
content: Identify the missing parts
Contact Lanco for the provision of replacement parts
actions: Contact Lanco with part numbers and descriptions
warnings: Always use genuine Lanco replacement parts
